note: Cities on the globe. status: live (built and in web/data/<id>) or planned. Planned entries list the open data to check first; none of them has been verified for this project yet.

cities.name: Sydney
cities.summary: Central Sydney: 7,962 buildings, the Opera House and Harbour Bridge, sun access on protected public places, and a game: walk it, ride the ferries, fly under the bridge.

cities.name: Melbourne
cities.summary: Central Melbourne from Docklands to the Shrine: 13,050 buildings on Geoscience Australia's 5 m LiDAR terrain, the Arts Centre spire, and sun on the public spaces the planning scheme protects.

cities.name: Melbourne Bayside
cities.summary: Port Phillip's shore from St Kilda to Brighton: 9,335 buildings, the 96 Brighton bathing boxes, Luna Park's Scenic Railway, and a game where little penguins come ashore on the St Kilda breakwater after sunset.

cities.name: New York
cities.data: NYC Open Data footprints with LiDAR roof heights; USGS 3DEP 1 m DEM; NYS orthoimagery.

cities.name: London
cities.data: Environment Agency 1 m LiDAR DTM (OGL); OSM heights; open aerial imagery still to find.

cities.name: Paris
cities.data: IGN RGE ALTI and BD ORTHO (open licence); BD TOPO building heights.

cities.name: Amsterdam
cities.data: AHN LiDAR; PDOK aerial imagery; 3D BAG building heights.

cities.name: Tokyo
cities.data: Project PLATEAU 3D city models (CC BY 4.0); GSI elevation tiles.

cities.name: Hong Kong
cities.summary: Victoria Harbour from Central to Tsim Sha Tsui and the Peak: 7,513 buildings, nearly all at the heights the Lands Department surveyed, checked against a 2020 LiDAR scan; the Bank of China Tower, HSBC and the Star Ferry; and a game: ride the ferry and the Peak Tram.

cities.name: Singapore
cities.data: OSM footprints and heights; open bare-earth DEM and imagery still to find.
